constraints: User approved Deep static analysis; never run target or allow-run
Keep credentials, cookies and personal profiles out of targets and records
Inspect only executable and packaged application artifacts
No strings/import absence proof; static evidence cannot establish runtime security or performance
No Ghidra-heavy call graph required; use bounded PE/archives/import/resources capabilities

brief.done_when: Version/hash-linked static findings with supporting evidence IDs, labelled confidence, important unknowns, plan states and a resumable handoff; export a report without full browser or performance claims.
brief.purpose: Establish evidence for source-to-artifact baseline, Rust implementation boundary, branding, footprint and architecture; complement source review and runtime tests.
brief.question: What PE structure, imports, resources and package composition are observed in the pinned Brave Windows artifacts and the built OpenSequoia Rust development executable, and what remains unknown about native components and feature exclusions?

findings.statement: OpenSequoia snapshot SHA256 6d7bde699288ce03570ac30e0e35e42a585681393fadf1449fba3ec2ebcfcccd contains two PE resources: RT_VERSION identifies ProductName OpenSequoia and FileVersion 0.1.0.0, and RT_MANIFEST requests asInvoker with PerMonitorV2 DPI awareness.

The inspected OpenSequoia snapshot PE header reports NX, PIE and high-entropy VA enabled, control_flow_guard false and code_signature null. These are static file flags, not proof of runtime sandboxing or security.

All 146 recorded OpenSequoia snapshot import rows were examined. Their library summary has 12 recorded names, including KERNEL32.dll/kernel32.dll case variants, USER32, GDI32, NTDLL, VCRUNTIME140 and Windows API-set CRT/synchronization DLL names; selected imports include CreateProcessW, CreateWindowExW, CreateFontW and TextOutW. Import tables do not establish absence of statically linked code or runtime-loaded dependencies.

Installed Brave brave.exe and chrome.dll both contain official-build version 158.1.100.58 and LastChange bd6d26d1bced03c17a98baa86d2cd3425d543d1b in their PE resources. The files are pinned separately by SHA256 eb7bdd6794feef543c70ed73db5a408636b9f0b86f6977609e8034b1f6da932f and be842bf3a479d88dfc1fdc4ef4cbb52589ff1de0b34259c5921cbd6489ddcf1f.

The downloaded standalone setup SHA256 2802553c89831effe624bd1b0dd8e39c463e03a1224d557441350a5586e559ce has updater PE version1.3.361.151 and ProductName BraveSoftware Update; resource B/102 occupies172883883bytes. Its wrapper metadata does not directly identify the embedded browser payload version.

The complete selected Brave version-folder inventory has377files and1146695025hashed file bytes. Largest contributors are Installer/chrome.7z569442764bytes and chrome.dll338606160bytes; the inventory covers installed files, not filesystem allocated clusters or profile data.

The installed baseline contains BraveVpnWireguardService/brave_vpn_wireguard_service.exe, tunnel.dll, wireguard.dll and brave_vpn_helper.exe with total24467776file bytes. These packaged VPN components support the authorized exclusion inventory; runtime service use and their contribution to startup/RAM were not measured here.

The final OpenSequoia executable SHA256930a4415a37137ad33ce77e4c82c134aa1ae0be5dcae14bc8449104ffb7042b8 advertises Control Flow Guard, NX, PIE and high-entropy VA. Its version/manifest resources still identify OpenSequoia0.1.0.0; code_signature is null. This is static metadata and does not establish production sandboxing or authentic signed updates.

Successive observed OpenSequoia build hashes differ, and the recorded PE control_flow_guard flag changes from false in6d7bde699288ce03570ac30e0e35e42a585681393fadf1449fba3ec2ebcfcccd to true in930a4415a37137ad33ce77e4c82c134aa1ae0be5dcae14bc8449104ffb7042b8. This confirms the final artifact flag; it is not a controlled performance comparison.

The first32observed bytes of updater resource B/102 are5d0000800078678a0a0000000000002abfeb5c8f2c0c6fbf98b98638c602eb80. The prefix is consistent with LZMA-Alone framing, an8MiB dictionary and declared176842616unpackedbytes; decompression validity and embedded browser file identities were not established.

The final development ZIP SHA256e1f6b22bb9f84113fc3f873e57a682d7b83cceb09936d083c172fc10b68183bf inventory is complete: opensequoia.exe908800bytes with SHA256930a4415a37137ad33ce77e4c82c134aa1ae0be5dcae14bc8449104ffb7042b8, LICENSE17099bytes, README.md2585bytes and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt322482bytes. The four members total1250966unpacked file bytes; no ZIP contradictions were reported.

hypotheses.claim: The OpenSequoia snapshot is a Windows x86_64 PE and its recorded import tables use documented Windows OS/CRT services.
notes: The PE architecture and complete recorded library summary match Windows/CRT service use. This supports import-table scope only, not absence of statically linked native code or runtime loads.
hypotheses.prediction: PE overview identifies x86_64/PE32+, and normal/delay/bound import summary lists OS service DLLs; any non-OS browser library would refute the import-table claim, but no import does not prove absence of static code.

hypotheses.claim: The current OpenSequoia snapshot does not yet provide complete Windows executable version/branding resources.
notes: The actual snapshot already contains OpenSequoia RT_VERSION and manifest resources; source expectations of missing metadata were stale after root rebuilt.
hypotheses.prediction: PE resource inventory lacks an OpenSequoia VS_VERSION_INFO or equivalent manifest/resource metadata; populated branding/version resource refutes this.

hypotheses.claim: The installed Brave executable and chrome.dll belong to the selected Brave 1.100.58 Windows baseline.
notes: Brave executable reports official build158.1.100.58; chrome.dll inspected resource also matches selected version. Hash-linked resource records pin installed bytes; source build flags remain separate.
hypotheses.prediction: Both PE version resources identify Brave/Chrome 158.1.100.58 or equivalent 1.100.58 release metadata; hashes pin actual installed bytes, and differing versions refute a shared installed baseline.

hypotheses.claim: The selected Brave standalone installer contains a large embedded compressed browser payload distinct from its installer code.
notes: Large embedded resource and compressed header observed, but exact browser payload content/version and decompression validation remain unknown; archive tool treats wrapper as a PE.
hypotheses.prediction: Its PE resource inventory or archive parser exposes a large compressed payload item; an unsupported container will leave extraction/composition unknown rather than imply no payload.

hypotheses.claim: The next OpenSequoia build will advertise Control Flow Guard after root adds the verified MSVC control-flow-guard compiler option.
notes: Final frozen build SHA930a4415...7042b8 has control_flow_guard true. Previous observed snapshot6d7bde69...cfcccd had false; source/build records are needed to attribute other changes or size delta.
hypotheses.prediction: The final rebuilt executable has a different SHA256 and native-layout-show reports control_flow_guard true; unchanged or false flag refutes the expected build-flag effect.

hypotheses.claim: chrome.dll is the largest file and a major contributor to the installed selected Brave version-folder footprint.
notes: Installer/chrome.7z is569442764bytes, larger than chrome.dll338606160bytes. chrome.dll remains a major contributor but is not the largest file.
hypotheses.prediction: A complete bounded inventory of that version folder ranks chrome.dll first and its byte size accounts for at least20percent of hashed file bytes; otherwise refute the dominance claim.

hypotheses.claim: The installed Brave baseline contains packaged VPN service binaries.
notes: Four VPN-named PE files are observed; their presence alone does not establish runtime activation/subscription behavior.
hypotheses.prediction: The version-folder inventory includes PE files under BraveVpnWireguardService or equivalent installed VPN service names; presence does not establish enabled runtime subscription behavior.

hypotheses.claim: Installer resource B/102 starts with an identifiable LZMA or archive framing header.
hypotheses.prediction: The first32bytes at observed resource RVA0x26824 plus observed PE image_base0x400000 show a recognizable compressed-stream header; otherwise compression format remains unknown.
